# CodePiper — Full Documentation

> Orchestrate multiple AI coding sessions from a single daemon.

CodePiper is an open-source remote orchestrator for managing multiple live interactive coding-agent sessions. Built with Bun + TypeScript. Everything runs locally on your machine — SQLite database, encrypted secrets, session data. No cloud accounts, no telemetry.

- GitHub: https://github.com/g3ortega/codepiper
- Documentation: https://g3ortega.github.io/codepiper/docs/
- Summary: https://g3ortega.github.io/codepiper/llms.txt

---

# Getting Started

## Quick Start

Get CodePiper running and create your first AI coding session in under 5 minutes.

### Prerequisites

- **Bun** v1.3.5 or later (the JavaScript runtime CodePiper is built on)
- **tmux** v3.0 or later (provides the terminal sessions your agents run inside)
- **At least one AI coding CLI**: Claude Code or Codex

Check everything with a single command:

```bash
codepiper doctor
```

### Install

```bash
npm i -g codepiper
```

Or install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/g3ortega/codepiper.git
cd codepiper
bun install
bun link
```

### Start the daemon

```bash
codepiper daemon --web
```

On first run, you'll see output like this:

```
✓ Daemon started on /tmp/codepiper.sock
✓ Web dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000
✓ Bootstrap password: k8f2-mN9x-pL3q
```

Save the bootstrap password. You'll need it to log in for the first time.

### Complete onboarding

Open `http://localhost:3000` in your browser. You'll be prompted to:

1. **Enter the bootstrap password** printed in your terminal
2. **Set a permanent password** for future logins
3. **Set up MFA**: scan the QR code with any authenticator app and enter the verification code

MFA is mandatory.

### Create your first session

From the CLI:

```bash
codepiper start -p claude-code -d ~/projects/my-app
```

From the web dashboard: go to Sessions → Create Session, choose your provider and working directory, click Create.

### Interact with your session

- **Web terminal**: Click on the session in the dashboard for live terminal view
- **CLI attach**: `codepiper attach <session-id>`
- **Send a prompt**: `codepiper send <session-id> "What is this project?"`

### Stop or resume

```bash
codepiper stop <session-id>
codepiper start --resume <session-id>
```

Sessions persist across daemon restarts.

---

## Installation

### System Requirements

| Dependency | Minimum Version | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| Bun | 1.3.5 | JavaScript runtime |
| tmux | 3.0 | Terminal session management |
| At least one AI coding CLI | Latest | The agent that runs inside sessions |

### Supported Platforms

| OS | Architecture |
|----|-------------|
| macOS (Darwin) | x64 (Intel), arm64 (Apple Silicon) |
| Linux | x64, arm64 |

Windows is not currently supported. Use WSL2 for Windows machines.

### Install Bun

```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```

### Install tmux

macOS: `brew install tmux`
Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install tmux`
Fedora/RHEL: `sudo dnf install tmux`

### Install a Provider

Claude Code (recommended):
```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

Codex CLI:
```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex
```

### Install CodePiper

```bash
npm i -g codepiper
```

### Verify Installation

```bash
codepiper doctor
```

---

## Your First Session

### Creating a Session

```bash
codepiper start -p claude-code -d ~/projects/my-app
```

Session options:
- `--billing api` — pay-per-token (required for automated workflows)
- `--worktree --create-branch feature/refactor` — git worktree isolation
- `--env-set my-api-keys` — attach encrypted environment variables
- `-- --model opus` — pass arguments to the provider

### Interacting

- **Web terminal**: Live xterm.js terminal with image paste support
- **CLI attach**: `codepiper attach <id>` (Ctrl+B D to detach)
- **Send text**: `codepiper send <id> "refactor the auth module"`
- **Send keys**: `codepiper keys <id> ctrl+c`
- **Send images**: `codepiper send <id> --image screenshot.png "what's wrong?"`

### Session Persistence

Sessions survive daemon restarts, SSH disconnects, laptop lid closes, and client disconnects. The daemon re-adopts orphaned tmux sessions on startup.

---

## Web Dashboard

The dashboard is a React SPA served by the daemon at `http://localhost:3000`.

### Pages

- **Sessions**: Create, list, and manage sessions with live terminal view
- **Analytics**: Token usage charts, model distribution, cache hit rate, cost estimation
- **Policies**: Create and manage permission rules, view audit log
- **Workflows**: Define and execute multi-session workflows
- **Settings**: Daemon config, workspaces, encrypted env sets, auth management

### Mobile PWA

Install as an app from your mobile browser. Push notifications alert you when sessions finish, crash, or need attention.

---

# Concepts

## Architecture Overview

CodePiper is a daemon-based orchestrator. A single long-running process manages all sessions, policies, analytics, and state.

```
CLI ──(unix socket)──▶ Daemon ──(tmux)──▶ Claude Code / Codex
Web UI ──(HTTP/WS)──▶  (Bun + SQLite)
```

### Key Services

| Service | Responsibility |
|---------|---------------|
| SessionManager | Spawn, stop, resume, and track provider sessions via tmux |
| PolicyEngine | Evaluate permission requests against rules, auto-handle decisions |
| WorkflowExecutor | Run multi-step YAML/JSON workflows across sessions |
| AuthService | Password + TOTP authentication, session tokens, rate limiting |
| TranscriptTailer | Parse Claude Code JSONL transcripts for token/tool analytics |
| EventBus | Route events from hooks, transcripts, and PTY to subscribers |

### Why tmux?

- Process isolation: each session runs in its own tmux session
- Persistence: tmux sessions survive daemon restarts and SSH disconnects
- Input fidelity: `tmux send-keys` is indistinguishable from physical keyboard input
- Output capture: `tmux capture-pane` provides terminal state for the web dashboard
- Universal: works with any provider that runs in a terminal

### Data Flow

Events flow from Claude Code hooks (structured events), transcript tailing (JSONL token/tool data), PTY capture (terminal output), and optional statusline heartbeats. All events are persisted to SQLite before processing ("persist first, process later").

### Permission Auto-Handling

1. Claude Code sends a PermissionRequest via hooks
2. PolicyEngine evaluates against matching rules
3. Decision stored in audit log
4. Allow: daemon sends "1"+Enter to tmux. Deny: "2"+Enter. Ask: surfaces to user.

---

## Sessions & Providers

A session is a running instance of an AI coding agent inside a tmux session named `codepiper-<uuid>`.

### Claude Code Provider

Full integration: native hooks, transcript tailing, model switching, dangerous mode, native-hooks policy channel, high analytics fidelity.

### Codex CLI Provider

Simpler integration: no hooks, no transcripts, no model switching, input-preflight policy channel, low analytics fidelity.

### Billing Modes

- **Subscription** (default): Scrubs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, uses Max plan billing. For interactive use.
- **API**: Preserves ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, pay-per-token. Required for automated workflows per Anthropic ToS.

### Model Switching (Claude Code)

```bash
codepiper model <id>         # Check current model
codepiper model <id> opus    # Switch to Opus
codepiper model <id> sonnet  # Switch to Sonnet
```

---

## Permission Policies

Control what AI agents can do with rule-based policies. Every decision is logged in an audit trail.

### Rule Structure

```json
{
  "action": "allow",
  "tool": "Read",
  "reason": "Reading files is always safe"
}
```

Actions: `allow`, `deny`, `ask`. Tool field supports glob patterns. Rules are evaluated in priority order; first match wins.

### Common Patterns

- Allow everything except destructive commands
- Read-only mode (allow Read/Glob/Grep/LS, deny everything else)
- Review all shell commands, allow everything else

### Policy Sets

Group related policies for easy assignment to sessions.

---

## Workflows

Chain multi-session tasks with YAML/JSON DSL.

### Step Types

- **session**: Spawn a session, send a prompt, wait for condition, extract results
- **if**: Conditional branching based on previous results
- **parallel**: Run multiple steps concurrently (wait modes: all, any, none)
- **foreach**: Loop over a list of items
- **log**: Output a message

### Wait Conditions

idle_prompt, permission_prompt, stop, event (Claude Code only), timeout (both providers).

### Error Handling

Strategies: fail (default), continue, retry (with configurable attempts and delay).

### Variable Substitution

`${...}` syntax for input variables, step results, and loop variables.

---

## Analytics & Tokens

Track token usage from every Claude Code session: prompt tokens, completion tokens, cache creation/read tokens, model distribution, tool usage.

### Cost Estimation

Per-model pricing tables applied to token counts. Separate rates for input, output, cache write, and cache read.

### Cache Hit Rate

```
cache_hit_rate = cache_read_tokens / (prompt_tokens + cache_creation_tokens + cache_read_tokens)
```

---

## Security Model

Single-user, self-hosted deployment. Five security layers:

1. **Transport**: Unix socket (CLI) or authenticated HTTP (web)
2. **Authentication**: Password (Argon2) + TOTP MFA (mandatory)
3. **Encryption**: AES-256-GCM for stored secrets
4. **Isolation**: API key scrubbing, session sandboxing
5. **Auditing**: Full decision trail for all policy actions

### Bootstrap Flow

Start daemon → prints bootstrap password → enter in browser → set password → set up MFA → normal login.

### Remote Access

Recommended: SSH tunnel. For persistent access: reverse proxy with TLS (Nginx or Caddy).

---

# Guides

## Multi-Device Setup

The daemon owns your sessions. Every client connects to the same daemon.

- Start from desktop CLI, check from phone, follow up from tablet, attach via SSH
- Local network: bind to `0.0.0.0`
- SSH tunnel: `ssh -L 3000:localhost:3000 -L 9999:localhost:9999 your-server`
- Mobile PWA: install from browser, get push notifications

## Remote Access

Multiple options: SSH tunnel (simplest), Tailscale (zero-config VPN), ngrok (quick public URL), Cloudflare Tunnel (production), Nginx/Caddy reverse proxy.

## Policy Configuration

Create policies via CLI, web dashboard, or API. Use policy sets to group rules. Set default action (ask/deny) for unmatched requests.

## Workflow Authoring

Define workflows in YAML with session steps, conditionals, parallel branches, loops, and variable extraction. Error handling with retry and continue strategies.

## PWA Installation

Install the dashboard as a native-like app from iOS Safari, Android Chrome, or desktop browsers.

---

# API Reference

## REST API

The daemon exposes HTTP endpoints over Unix socket (CLI) and HTTP port (web dashboard, prefixed with `/api`).

### Sessions (11 endpoints)
GET /sessions, POST /sessions, GET /sessions/:id, POST /sessions/:id/stop, POST /sessions/:id/kill, POST /sessions/:id/resume, POST /sessions/:id/send, POST /sessions/:id/keys, GET /sessions/:id/output, POST /sessions/:id/resize, POST /sessions/:id/upload-image

### Policies (5 endpoints)
GET /policies, POST /policies, GET /policies/:id, PUT /policies/:id, DELETE /policies/:id

### Policy Sets (8 endpoints)
CRUD + member management + audit log

### Analytics (7 endpoints)
GET /analytics/overview, /activity-timeline, /token-usage, /tokens-by-model, /sessions-by-provider, /tool-usage, /policy-decisions

### Git (9 endpoints per session)
Status, branches, log, diff, file, file-raw, diff-stat, stage, unstage

### Workflows (10 endpoints)
CRUD + execute, executions, cancel

### Auth (11 endpoints)
Status, setup, login, logout, password, MFA setup/verify, sessions, revoke-all, CLI-only reset operations

### Settings (13 endpoints)
Daemon settings, workspaces, environment sets

## WebSocket Protocol

WebSocket server on port 9999. Topics: session output, session events, all sessions, workflow execution progress. Supports PTY input over WebSocket.

## CLI Commands

daemon, start, stop, kill, resize, sessions, attach, send, keys, slash, tail, model, policy, policy-set, audit, analytics, providers, workspace, env-set, logs, doctor, workflow, auth, hook-forward (internal).

---

# Contributing

## Development Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/g3ortega/codepiper.git
cd codepiper
bun install
bun run daemon:web  # Start with web dashboard
```

Code quality: Biome (double quotes, semicolons, 2-space indent, 100 char line width).

## Adding a Provider

Implement the Provider interface: startSession, sendText, sendKeys, stopSession, onEvent. Optional: switchModel, getCurrentModel. Declare capabilities. Register in the provider registry.

## Testing

```bash
bun test              # All tests
bun test --coverage   # With coverage
bun run pre-commit    # Full quality check (lint + typecheck + tests)
```
